references.text: The context for leprosy in clothing, which mentions wool and linen garments, as verse 48 continues to elaborate on with warp and weft
Describes what should be done with the garment that has leprosy, whether it is in the warp or weft, in wool or linen, or in any leather work
Summarizes the law concerning leprosy in garments of wool or linen, in warp or weft, and in leather work
Mentions linen (שֵׁשׁ) as a material in the tabernacle's curtain, relevant for understanding textile materials in the Mosaic Law
Prohibition against mixing wool and linen in the same garment, showing the importance of distinguishing between these materials mentioned in Leviticus 13:48
